title: Add local observability verification script (spans + metrics sanity checks)
author: Sabrina James
release_notes: Examples: add `scripts/verify_observability.py` to validate local OTel collector is receiving spans/metrics and to surface common misconfigurations (endpoint, headers, collector ports).
description: Title: Add local observability verification script (spans + metrics sanity checks) Summary: Adds a small helper script to verify that example apps are actually emitting traces and basic runtime metrics during local development. This is meant to reduce the current “it runs but I can’t see anything in my collector/Console” loop when folks are trying the RAG/agent examples or quickstart-aligned instrumentation patterns. Motivation / Context: During internal beta testing for quickstart templates and the refactors in redwood-examples, the most common failure mode we saw was misconfigured local OTel collection (wrong OTLP port, collector not running, exporter auth set when it shouldn’t be, or traces going to stdout with no obvious success signal). This PR adds an opinionated, low-ceremony sanity check that: (1) makes a single request against a running example server, (2) checks local collector Prometheus metrics for accepted spans/metrics, and (3) prints actionable remediations when it can’t verify. Intended use: local development only (not CI by default). What’s included: - New script: `scripts/verify_observability.py` - Validates env (non-fatal warnings): `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT` (default http://localhost:4318), `REDWOOD_API_KEY` presence (without printing), `REDWOOD_MODEL` (optional). - Performs a basic HTTP request to the example app health endpoint (configurable) and optionally triggers a generation endpoint if provided. - Polls the collector Prometheus endpoint (default http://localhost:8888/metrics) for a short window and checks for counters incrementing: `otelcol_receiver_accepted_spans` or `otelcol_receiver_accepted_traces` (collector-version dependent), plus at least one of `otelcol_exporter_sent_spans` / `otelcol_exporter_sent_metric_points`. - Outputs a clear PASS/FAIL plus next steps (e.g., “collector not reachable”, “wrong OTLP endpoint/port”, “prometheus endpoint disabled”, “app not instrumented / OTEL_* not set”). - Redaction: never prints API keys, headers, or full URLs containing credentials. - Small doc updates: wire the script into the local dev instructions for the observability-enabled examples. Example usage: `python3 scripts/verify_observability.py --app-url http://localhost:8080 --collector-metrics-url http://localhost:8888/metrics --timeout-seconds 20` or `python3 scripts/verify_observability.py --app-url http://localhost:8080 --trigger-path /chat` (if the example exposes a cheap request path that generates at least one span). Key implementation notes: - Collector metrics parsing is intentionally shallow (regex + float parsing) rather than pulling in Prometheus client deps, to keep the examples repo lightweight. - We treat “collector metrics endpoint not available” as a distinct error with instructions to enable the Prometheus exporter in docker-compose (templates/quickstarts are also standardizing on 8888 for local). - We avoid tagging anything new on requests; this script is purely “does anything flow” and doesn’t add dimensions/attributes that could increase cardinality. Changed files (high level): - `scripts/verify_observability.py` (new) - `scripts/README.md` (new short doc for scripts folder) - `rag/README.md` (add “Verify observability” step) - `agents/README.md` (add “Verify observability” step) - `docker-compose.otel.local.yml` (document Prometheus endpoint + ensure 8888 is exposed in the local example compose) - `Makefile` (add `make verify-otel APP_URL=...`) Illustrative snippet (from `scripts/verify_observability.py`): `def metric_value(text: str, name: str) -> float: pattern = rf"^{re.escape(name)}\{{.*\}}\s+([0-9\.eE+-]+)$" for line in text.splitlines(): m = re.match(pattern, line) if m: return float(m.group(1)) return 0.0` and `accepted_before = max(metric_value(metrics, "otelcol_receiver_accepted_spans"), metric_value(metrics, "otelcol_receiver_accepted_traces")) ... accepted_after = ... if accepted_after <= accepted_before: fail("No accepted spans observed", hint=["Ensure OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT points at the collector (default http://localhost:4318)", "Ensure the example app is running with instrumentation enabled", "Check collector logs for exporter errors"])` Test plan: - Manual: run `docker compose -f docker-compose.otel.local.yml up` and start `rag` example locally; run `make verify-otel APP_URL=http://localhost:8080` and confirm PASS with counters increasing. - Manual negative cases: stop collector (script should report collector unreachable); point to wrong OTLP endpoint (collector metrics show no increments); disable prometheus exporter (script should explain how to enable / expose 8888). - CI: linting (ruff) and basic import check is included; script isn’t executed in CI to avoid network flakiness. Open questions / follow-ups: - If we standardize the collector metrics endpoint differently across repos, we should update defaults in templates + examples together. For now we align to 8888 based on current quickstart-local conventions (see ENG-4184 notes). - If collector metric names drift again, the script checks multiple options but may need periodic updates; kept small intentionally. Review notes / discussion: - Allison requested that we avoid parsing span payloads or relying on logs, and instead use collector counters; implemented. - Sergio requested we keep the metric checks tolerant across collector versions (accepted_traces vs accepted_spans); implemented. - Monica requested we add remediation text specific to Redwood request-id propagation only when relevant; we kept it generic but added a hint to confirm `x-redwood-request-id` shows up in app logs if users have that enabled. Merge: Squash merged into `main`.
commits: docs: add verify step to rag + agents READMEs
chore: add Makefile target for verify-otel
chore: document/promote collector metrics endpoint (8888) for local compose
review_conversation: Allison Grant: Can we avoid relying on collector logs? Folks run collectors in different modes and logs are noisy. Prefer checking collector Prometheus metrics and being tolerant to metric name changes across versions.
Sabrina James (author): Ack. Updated to poll /metrics and look for receiver accepted + exporter sent counters. Also added accepted_traces fallback for older collectors.
Sergio Costa: Please keep the checks minimal—this should be a sanity check, not a full diagnostics tool. Also watch out for high-cardinality parsing of metric labels.
Sabrina James (author): Yep—only reads the numeric values and ignores labels entirely (regex matches any labelset). No span attribute parsing.
Monica Patel: Can we make the remediation text explicit about the OTLP ports? People frequently use 4317 vs 4318 incorrectly.
Sabrina James (author): Added explicit hints: HTTP/proto defaults to 4318; gRPC is 4317. Script prints the configured endpoint and suggests swapping if unreachable.
Sahana Iyer: CI looks good. Please ensure the script exits non-zero on failure (so devs can wire it into a preflight).
Sabrina James (author): Updated to exit(2) on failures and exit(0) on success; added `--json` option request to backlog (not included).
